eventMetadata.context_description: Recent MetService New Zealand forecasts and ensemble guidance position a daytime maximum of 16 °C as the most probable outcome for Wellington on 22 May, reflecting mild northerly flow that advects warmer air from subtropical latitudes ahead of an approaching cold front. Partial high cloud cover is expected to moderate surface heating and keep readings from climbing into the upper teens, consistent with the city’s May climatology where daily highs average 14–16 °C and rarely exceed 19 °C. Model consensus remains tight around this range, with only modest spread arising from uncertainties in frontal timing and boundary-layer mixing; probabilities drop sharply above 17 °C or below 15 °C given the absence of strong subtropical advection or clear-sky radiative conditions. The next high-resolution model cycle tonight should further refine these projections ahead of the official observation window.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent India Meteorological Department forecasts highlight persistent pre-monsoon heat across Uttar Pradesh, with clear skies, weak westerly winds, and heat-wave conditions expected to push Lucknow’s maximum temperature on May 22 toward 42–45 °C. Official guidance lists a 45 °C high under these synoptic patterns, yet historical variability in May maxima—typically 40–44 °C—keeps the 41 °C-or-below and 42 °C outcomes nearly tied in trader pricing. Model consensus shows limited moisture influx, reducing cloud cover and favoring higher readings, while any late-day western disturbance could cap temperatures closer to 41 °C. Resolution hinges on the verified IMD observation at the Lucknow station, with updated model runs tomorrow morning likely to sharpen the market’s assessment of this narrow range.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day by the Forecast for the Ninoy Aquino International Airport Station once information is finalized, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/ph/manila/RPLL.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve to "Yes" until all data for this date has been finalized.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Any revisions to temperatures recorded after data is finalized for this market's timeframe will not be considered for this market's resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent warmer-than-normal conditions across Metro Manila, driven by the tail end of the dry season and limited cloud cover, have kept daily maximum temperatures near 35–37 °C, aligning with PAGASA’s seasonal outlook for above-average heat. Official station readings from the past week show afternoon peaks of 34–36 °C under partly cloudy skies with light winds that reduce mixing and allow urban heat-island effects to intensify. Forecast models indicate continued stable high-pressure influence through May 23, with only modest chances of isolated showers that could briefly limit afternoon heating. This narrow range of expected outcomes explains the closely matched market-implied probabilities for 36 °C and 37 °C, as traders weigh small differences in wind speed, humidity, and timing of any convective activity.
